clue.text: Unusually large bouncer

definitions.meaning: a ... crop or ... issue is one of exceptional size
in cricket a bouncer is a short ball that rears up at the batsman

explanation.surface: A doorman of unusual size stands at a club entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' looks like a nightclub doorman; it is the cricket ball also called a BUMPER, a fast delivery pitched short so it rises high.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an exceptionally big harvest is called bumper, and cricket uses the word for a short-pitched rising delivery.

clue.text: HQ has to appraise cost of borrowing

parts.note: headquarters is a base of operations
to appraise is to rate or value

explanation.surface: Head office must assess what loans will cost.
explanation.definitionFit: The central bank's lending figure is the benchmark interest charge that sets what loans cost.

clue.text: Isn't Amy a remarkable support?

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a woman named Amy is a wonderful help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges ISNTAMYA, the letters of 'Isn't Amy a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief prop or pillar on which something depends, originally a ship's principal rope.

clue.text: In severe pain all the time

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone suffers acute pain constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, at every moment, as in 'ever hopeful'.

clue.text: Must one intrude upon English lawmen by force?

indicators.note: intrude upon says one group of letters pushes its way into the middle of another

parts.note: MPs, Members of Parliament, are the people who make laws
has, as in 'has to', means must
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question whether someone must barge in on English legislators by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrude upon' puts HAS + I inside MPS, after E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is stress or forcefulness given to words or ideas, so force is a fair synonym.

clue.text: MD in the drink!

parts.note: MD reads as managing director, the man at the head of the board; if he ends up in the drink he has fallen off a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The cry raised when someone falls from a vessel into the sea, which the clue renders as a board member in the water.

clue.text: Shock caused by hospital broadcast

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs
to broadcast a programme is to air it

explanation.surface: A trauma brought about by a radio programme about a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like the trauma; it is a shock of hair, a thick mass on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick bushy mass of hair on someone's head.

clue.text: Stopped after being restrained

definitions.meaning: ... means remained or halted, as in ... put
to stay something is to check or hold it back, as in staying a hand or an execution

explanation.surface: Someone halted after being held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: remained in place, and checked or held back, as a judge stays proceedings.

clue.text: Sack German gent in the Seychelles

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
Herr is the German word for a gentleman, Mr

explanation.surface: A German man is dismissed while on the Seychelles islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal; it is an old word for white fortified wine from Spain, as drunk by Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack was the Elizabethan name for dry white wines from Spain and the Canaries, the forerunner of today's fortified Spanish wine.

clue.text: Go to pieces in quiet bucks. Town

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
Iver is a village town in Buckinghamshire, Bucks for short

explanation.surface: Someone falls apart in a peaceful town in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is the short name of Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London; the full stop disguises 'Bucks.' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver can mean to shatter or break into fragments, as in 'shiver my timbers'.

clue.text: Consider if engineer must carry permit to travel east

indicators.note: must carry tells us one piece holds another within it

parts.note: a visa is an official permit to enter a country
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an engineer needs travel documents for a trip eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must carry' puts VISA inside ENG, and E for east follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage is to picture or contemplate a possibility, which is to consider it.

clue.text: Don once set on becoming the world's best

indicators.note: becoming says these letters change into something new

explanation.surface: A university lecturer once set his heart on being the top in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges DONONCESETON, the letters of 'Don once set on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second to none has no superior anywhere, so it is the finest there is.

clue.text: Overcharge when sudden demand occurs

definitions.meaning: informal for charging them too much
a ... is a sudden surge of buyers, as in a ... on the banks

explanation.surface: Prices are inflated when there is a sudden surge of buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to fleece a customer; and a sudden heavy demand for goods, as in the Christmas crush.

clue.text: Sounds like you and I have to do basketwork

indicators.note: Sounds like says the letters are spoken, giving a word heard the same way

parts.note: you and I together are we, so 'you and I have' is we've

explanation.surface: Two people say they must take up wickerwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketwork is made by interlacing strands of cane or willow, which is weaving.

clue.text: Hardly an animal one can carry

definitions.meaning: a large furry carnivore such as a grizzly
to ... a load is to carry it

explanation.surface: A large beast is hardly something a person could carry about.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the animal is far too big to carry, yet its name also means to carry; 'Hardly' and 'one can' only link the two.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the big shaggy mammal; the verb means to hold up or convey a weight.

clue.text: Escort Ayesha into Iraqi city

indicators.note: into places one piece within the other

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city in what is now Iraq
Ayesha is the heroine of H. Rider Haggard's novel She, so she is She

explanation.surface: A man accompanies a woman named Ayesha into an Iraqi city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayesha, 'She-who-must-be-obeyed', is the title character of Haggard's adventure novel She.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher escorts guests to their seats at a wedding or theatre, so to usher is to escort.

clue.text: At liberty to be promiscuous

definitions.meaning: an animal on the ... is free
a ... person, in the old phrase, has lax morals

explanation.surface: Someone free to sleep around.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: unconfined and free, and morally lax in old-fashioned usage.

clue.text: It's just your luck that there's nothing left

definitions.meaning: a phrase said meaning that is your share of fortune, take it or leave it
the same phrase said meaning you have had everything there is

explanation.surface: Bad luck: everything has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means that is all you get: your allotted portion, with no more remaining.

clue.text: Hit out at a sluggard

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to attack them with blows on all sides

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out at an idle person.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb, to strike out wildly in every direction; as one word, an idler who avoids work.

clue.text: Monarch arranged meeting with military body

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A king organises a gathering with an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges MEETING into EGIMENT, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent army unit, usually commanded by a colonel.

clue.text: Those fated as possible world leaders

indicators.note: possible suggests one of several possible arrangements of these letters

explanation.surface: People whom destiny might make rulers of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges THOSEFATEDAS, the letters of 'Those fated as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidents and monarchs are the formal chief representatives of countries.

clue.text: Rumpus when priest heads conciliation service

indicators.note: heads means one piece goes in front of the other

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ACAS is Britain's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when a clergyman runs a peace-making body.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the UK body that mediates in industrial disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or brawl, which is a rumpus.

clue.text: Only embrace airman to offer comfort

indicators.note: embrace says one piece wraps round another

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
AC is aircraftman, the lowest rank in the RAF

explanation.surface: Just hug a pilot to console him.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in distress, so to offer it is to give comfort.

clue.text: Cross when a small marsupial died

parts.note: roo is a short word for a kangaroo, a marsupial
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Anger at a little kangaroo's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the noun, a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

clue.text: I cut into additional fabric

indicators.note: cut into says one piece slices its way inside the other

parts.note: more means extra or additional

explanation.surface: Someone takes scissors to some extra cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Moire is a silk with a rippled watered pattern, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Exclude Irish leader from Italian port

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Irish politician is refused entry to a harbour in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a major seaport on the Adriatic coast of Apulia in southern Italy.

clue.text: Show of humour when embracing second gear

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A comic performance in which a second set of equipment is used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when embracing' only links the definition to the wordplay; S and KIT stand side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch or parody.

clue.text: Putting the head in charge is fair

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other piece

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Appointing the boss as leader is only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like an adjective meaning just; it is the noun, an outdoor festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair with stalls and games, often held to raise money.

clue.text: Top-class shot, but quite mad

parts.note: crack troops are expert or first-rate
a pot is a shot, as in snooker or a potshot

explanation.surface: An expert marksman who is nonetheless completely insane.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, used adjectivally of hare-brained ideas.

clue.text: Architectural feature drives yours truly to drink

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying me
to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Some building detail is so irritating it makes the writer turn to alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A metope is the square panel between triglyphs in a Doric frieze, a classical building element.

clue.text: Succulent vegetable in bloom

parts.note: succulent fruit is sweet and juicy
a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A juicy vegetable in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing plant grown for its fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Parisian is accepted by band of players

annotationWithheld.why: Parisian is accepted by band of players (6): EST inside SET gives SESTET, but 'band' must give SET and also be part of the definition 'band of players'; no other word supplies SET, so a word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Parisian is accepted by band of players
